column3: NOT a wood specimen: the whole loss of real marimba bars on their own frame, wood, cord and radiation together, with the resonators off; an unrefereed student report from a room recording. H. Hill, Exponential Time Decay Constants of Marimba Bars, NSF REU final report, University of Illinois Physics 406, summer 2011 (adviser S. Errede): a Yamaha YM-5100A five-octave marimba, bars C2 to C7, struck at center, off-center and edge, recorded with and without the resonators; eta = 1/(pi tau f) from exponential fits on f1, f4, f10 and f20 without the resonators. Wood: Honduras rosewood, per the maker's spec for that model (the report says only rosewood)
column4: The printed mean as it stands: 'The average η value is η = 0.0045 ± 0.0009'; the printed range 0.0036 to 0.0068 is the limit. The report finds tau proportional to 1/f, so eta is one number for every mode: 1/tau = pi eta f, the loss_factor row with gamma_B and the viscoelastic constant both zero. No value is read off its figures
column5: Tried after seeing that the marimba pages decay too fast on the fit3 law (D. latifolia beam values, wood alone); no recording number enters. bar_strike puts no other damping on a bar alone (no supports; the receiver transfers only observe), so radiation and the cord are counted once, inside eta; a tube adds only its own wall and open-end losses, which eta was measured without
